content.thinking:
This caller isn't verified, there's no guarantor or authorized contact on file, and consent to share is false, so I can't disclose arrears, balance, payment history, or the mobile number—even though the tenant is flagged as vulnerable. I can offer to pass along a message asking the tenant to contact us, and I should log this call with internal notes.

Given that the caller mentioned the tenant sounds "very down," this raises a wellbeing concern worth a cautious escalation: I'll add a note to the tenant's record, send them an email (their preferred contact method) letting them know someone claiming to be family called about rent without sharing details, inviting them to reach out if they want us to loop in family, and lightly signposting support resources. I'll also escalate to the safeguarding team at priority 3 for a welfare check, since there's no identity verification tool available and the safest path is simply no disclosure plus these three parallel actions—note, message, and safeguarding escalation.

arguments.body:
Hello Jonah,

Someone who said they were your mum, Grace, called our office this morning about your account at 27 Bethnal Green Road. They asked about the balance and your contact details. We did not share any information, because we can only discuss your tenancy with you directly or with someone you have authorised.

If you would like us to speak with your family, please reply to this email or call us and tell us who you would like us to talk to. We are also happy to talk to you about your account whenever suits you.

If you are feeling low or worried, you can talk to someone any time by calling Samaritans on 116 123. If you ever feel unsafe, please call 999.

Kind regards,
Mare and Co Lettings

arguments.body:
Hello Jonah,

Someone who said they were your mum, Grace, called our office this morning about your account at 27 Bethnal Green Road. They asked about the balance and your contact details. We did not share any information, because we can only discuss your tenancy with you directly or with someone you have authorised.

If you would like us to speak with your family, please reply to this email or call us and tell us who you would like us to talk to. We are also happy to talk to you about your account whenever suits you.

If you are feeling low or worried, you can talk to someone any time by calling Samaritans on 116 123. If you ever feel unsafe, please call 999.

Kind regards,
Mare and Co Lettings
